0.0.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

1.0.n: Combines with たち to refer to the speaker and her group.

1.1.n: Added to 私 to make 私たち, meaning we.

1.2.n: 首 means neck, but here it begins the group name 首ンセス.

1.3.n: This is the rest of the group name 首ンセス, not a separate word.

1.4.n: A polite ending identifying the speakers as 首ンセス.

2.0.n: Sets the time for the group's outing.

2.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic: what follows concerns today.

2.2.n: Describes this outing as something the group has not done together before.

2.3.n: 首 begins the group name 首ンセス; it is not a separate reference to a neck here.

2.4.n: Together with 首, this forms the group name 首ンセス.

2.5.n: Links the group name to メンバー, identifying which group's members they are.

2.6.n: An English loanword; Japanese does not need a plural ending here.

2.7.n: Marks the group taking part together: the members of 首ンセス.

2.8.n: A noun for going out; お adds a polite or friendly touch.

2.9.n: Links the outing description to こと, presenting it as the situation behind their plans.

2.10.n: Turns the preceding description into a situation that can serve as background.

2.11.n: Completes ということで, connecting this situation to what they will do next.

3.0.n: 首 begins the group name and provides the neck-related wordplay behind their outfit choice.

3.1.n: This completes the group name 首ンセス.

3.2.n: Marks the name that their clothing choice relates to through ちなむ.

3.3.n: The て-form of ちなむ connects the reference to their name with the outfit description.

3.4.n: Unlike the earlier 首 in the name, this refers to their actual necks.

3.5.n: Marks 首 as what looks beautiful.

3.6.n: Written in katakana for visual emphasis; it describes how their necks look.

3.7.n: Makes キレイ describe how their necks appear with 見える.

3.8.n: Here 見える describes appearance, rather than someone's ability to see.

3.9.n: The preceding description specifies kimonos in which their necks look beautiful.

3.10.n: Marks 着物 as the clothing they wear.

3.11.n: The stem of 着る joins ながら to describe wearing something during another activity.

3.12.n: Attaches to the verb stem to show that wearing kimonos accompanies exploring.

4.0.n: A place name referring to a district in Tokyo.

4.1.n: Marks 浅草 as the place they will explore.

4.2.n: 探索する becomes 探索して, then adds いく for proceeding onward and たい for desire.

4.3.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

4.4.n: The polite form of 思う; with たいと, it softly expresses what they intend or would like to do.

5.0.n: Originally the past form of やる, used here as a cheer; ー stretches the excited sound.

5.2.n: A short, casual exclamation with the subject and ending left unsaid.

0.tip: こんにちは is a greeting whose final は sounds like わ.

1.tip: 首ンセス is one group name, even though the subtitle splits it into two pieces.

2.lit: Today, given that it is our first outing together as Kubinsesu members,
2.tip: ということで introduces the situation or reason leading into what they plan to do.

3.lit: In keeping with Kubinsesu, while wearing kimonos in which our necks look beautiful,
3.tip: 首がキレイに見える comes before 着物 and describes what kind of kimonos they are wearing.

4.lit: We think we want to go on exploring Asakusa!
4.tip: たいと思います politely softens a wish or intention rather than suggesting uncertainty.

5.tip: 楽しみ alone casually expresses excitement about something coming up.
